brief: A small display stand: three bases meeting at a corner with a raised platform on a spike at that corner.

requirements.evidence: Three level-0 full bases (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full) form a compact triangular stand; the purpose is shown by the raised platform, but no prop could be staged on the platform because the configurator does not offer the spike/platform as a prop surface.

requirements.requirement: Three bases meeting at a corner
requirements.evidence: Bases at 0,0,0 / 1,0,0 / 0,1,0 all touch the junction 0,0|0,1|1,0; get_build lists them as one group.

requirements.requirement: Raised platform on a spike at that corner
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 fitted as a mount spike at that exact junction, with setSpikeAccessory platform-lrg applied (budget rose to 5 parts); check_build meshClash clear. House rules also applied: capOpenFaces (12 caps) and lockJoints (3 joint bolts).

finish.summary: Built a small triangular display stand: three full bases at 0,0 / 1,0 / 0,1 meeting at one corner, a mount spike at that junction carrying a large raised platform, open faces capped and joints locked. Verified with check_build (no issues, meshClash clear). The platform itself is not a prop surface in the configurator, so no display object was staged on it.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your corner display stand — three bases meeting at a point, with a raised platform on the spike there. I'll check the current build and locate that corner.

result.note: A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

warnings.message: 1 part(s) could slide apart (1 piece(s)); joint bolts lock them.
2 part(s) could slide apart (2 piece(s)); joint bolts lock them.

offersNear.note: Open offers at the base just added (valid until the next change): apply one by its socket, no find_sockets needed.

events.text: The spike is up at the corner. Now I'll fit its raised platform.

result.note: A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

outcomes.message: a solid spike cannot carry a platform; only a mount spike can: details.steps fits a mount spike on the same junction, then the platform.
a solid spike cannot carry a platform; only a mount spike can: details.steps fits a mount spike on the same junction, then the platform.

result.rollback: Nothing in this batch is on the build: one op was refused, so every op in it was undone. Fix or drop the refused op and send the batch again (a refusal with details.steps gives the whole batch with it fixed: send those ops as one apply); refs and offers from this batch do not exist.

events.text: Three bases meet at the corner with the mount spike and large platform fitted. Now I'll cap the open faces, lock the joints, and check the platform as a display surface.

outcomes.message: props stand on a piece, cover, cap, bin or drawer, or in a bolt-on, notch or bay bin; not on a spike.

result.note: ok covers rule errors only. meshClash must read "clear" for the meshes to be checked and clear.
